artifacts.summary: 5-phase implementation discriminating orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (d) absent-handoff branch on recover_json's .reason, adding a RECOVERY_DECLINED defect class attributed to the dispatched agent's own file, and first repairing a predecessor regression in the fixture suite (110/110 -> 127/127 passed after the extension).

completion_data.completion_summary: Discriminated orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (d) branch on recover_json's .reason so a declined return-meta recovery with a status-shaped cause (STATUS_IN_PROGRESS/STATUS_NOT_SUCCESS/META_DISPATCH_SEQ_MISMATCH) records a new RECOVERY_DECLINED defect attributed to the dispatched agent's own file, while the nothing-produced case (META_MISSING) keeps the original HANDOFF_STALE_OR_ABSENT behavior attributed to skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md unchanged. Also repaired a predecessor regression that had silently broken 34 of 110 fixtures in the test suite (missing sandbox lib copy), restoring it as a reliable regression guard before extending it to 127 passing fixtures covering all three sub-cases.

memory_candidates.content: Regression-proof technique for a test-suite extension: after adding new/extended fixtures that assert a behavior change, temporarily restore the PRE-fix version of the production file (e.g. via `git show <pre-fix-commit>:path > path`), rerun the suite, and confirm the new/extended assertions flip red (never green) before restoring the fix. This proves the new fixtures genuinely exercise the change rather than passing tautologically (e.g. asserting a count that happens to already be zero). Concretely used: reverting orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (d) discrimination flipped exactly 9 of the newly-added/extended assertions from pass to fail, confirming they were load-bearing.

When a diagnostic branch collapses 'nothing was produced' and 'something was produced but rejected' into one defect class/attribution, the attribution is systematically wrong for the second sub-case: an agent-side artifact that exists and was read gets blamed on the orchestrator/caller instead of the agent that produced it. The fix pattern is to discriminate on an already-available diagnostic field (here, orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh's `.reason`, distinct from the always-'NONE' `evidence_reason` field that looks similar but never discriminates on the recovered=false path) rather than adding a new detector — the data needed to route correctly was already being computed and discarded.
